page.title: Hybrid Event Production Services Explained
page.description: Learn what hybrid event production covers, from platform selection and venue AV to staffing, timelines, backup streams, and post-event deliverables.
page.h1: What is included in hybrid event production services?
page.definition: Hybrid event production services are end-to-end management of events that combine in-person and virtual audiences, covering platform selection, venue AV integration, live streaming, speaker rehearsals, run-of-show execution, backup streams, real-time moderation, recording, editing, post-event analytics delivery, and attendee engagement tools for sponsors and stakeholders.
page.quick_answer: Start by locking the venue AV and streaming platform six to eight weeks out, then assign a show caller, speaker manager, and platform operator to own the run of show and backup stream. West Peek Productions produces virtual, hybrid and webinar events and sets up marketing, content and creative operations.

sections.h2: What does a hybrid event production package include?

blocks.p: A full package covers platform configuration, venue AV integration, speaker rehearsals, live production, backup streaming, moderation, recording, editing, and post-event analytics.

ul: Platform setup and branding on Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, or StreamYard
Venue AV coordination: program feed, audio embed, camera switching, and encoder connection
Speaker brief, slide template, lower thirds, and one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before
Live producer, Q&A moderation, and dedicated backup stream on a separate internet connection
Edited recording, highlight clips, engagement report, and attendee data export

sections.h2: How do you choose the right platform and venue AV?

blocks.p: Match the platform to your audience size and interaction needs, then verify the venue AV can output a clean program feed to the encoder.

sections.h2: What staffing roles are needed for a hybrid event?

blocks.p: Summits and hybrid events need a show caller, speaker manager, moderator, and platform operator, while a simple webinar can run with one producer.

ul: Show caller: owns run of show, cues cameras, graphics, and transitions
Speaker manager: coordinates green room, tech checks, and speaker flow
Moderator: fields audience questions, manages chat, and relays to stage
Platform operator: monitors stream health, recording, and backup encoder
AV liaison: bridges venue crew and production team for signal integrity

sections.h2: What is the typical timeline and lead time?

blocks.p: Plan a hybrid conference six to eight weeks out; lock the venue AV and the platform before the agenda is final.

A webinar moves in three to four weeks from brief to live. The critical path: platform and venue contracts week one, speaker confirmations and slide deck freeze week two, full rehearsal week three, technical check sixty minutes before go-live. Allow two to three weeks from brief to live for a repeat format; a first-time summit needs the full window.

sections.h2: How are backup streams and failover handled?

blocks.p: A dedicated backup encoder runs in parallel on a separate internet connection, ready to switch within seconds if the primary stream drops.

The platform operator monitors both streams on a confidence monitor. If the primary fails, the show caller cuts to backup with a single keystroke. The venue AV team provides a redundant program feed from a second switcher output. Test the failover during rehearsal so the switch is seamless and recorded.

sections.h2: What deliverables should you expect after the event?

blocks.p: Deliverables include an edited recording, highlight clips, engagement reports, attendee data, and a post-event debrief document.

ul: Full edited recording uploaded to your platform within 24 to 48 hours
Three to five highlight clips optimized for social media
Engagement report: attendance curve, poll results, Q&A volume, chat sentiment
Attendee list with registration fields and engagement scores for CRM import
Debrief document: what worked, technical notes, and recommendations for next event

faq.q: How much does hybrid event production cost?
faq.a: Moderated webinars range from $2,500 to $7,500 per production, while executive summits and hybrid conferences start at $10,000 and scale upward based on complexity, venues, and attendee count.

faq.q: Can we use our existing platform like Zoom or Teams?
faq.a: Yes, production teams work on the platform you already use, such as Zoom Webinars, Microsoft Teams, ON24, or StreamYard, and configure it for hybrid delivery. They handle platform settings, branding, and integration with your registration system.

faq.q: What is the difference between platform and production?
faq.a: The platform is software for streaming and registration; production is the crew, cameras, encoder, run of show, and backup stream that make the event run smoothly. You purchase both separately, and the production team operates the platform on event day.

faq.q: How soon do we get the replay and analytics?
faq.a: Send the replay within 24 to 48 hours while attendees still remember the event, and deliver engagement reports and attendee data within one week for follow-up campaigns. Edited highlight clips for social media arrive in the same window.
